problem:
Let $v=[\begin{aligned}x \\ 2x \\ 4 \\ -5\end{aligned}]$ and $w=[\begin{aligned}3x \\ -3 \\ x \\ 2\end{aligned}].$
If $v\cdot w=-2$ and $x>0$, find the value of $x.$
worked_solution:
Starting from the equation $v\cdot w=-2,$ we compute the dot product in terms of $x$ and then solve for $x$ in the resulting equation:

$$
\begin{aligned}v\cdot w & =-2 \\ x\cdot 3x+2x\cdot (-3)+4\cdot x+(-5)\cdot 2 & =-2 \\ 3{x}^{2}-6x+4x-10 & =-2 \\ 3{x}^{2}-2x-8 & =0\end{aligned}
$$

Now, using the quadratic formula, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}x & =\frac{-(-2)\pm \sqrt{(-2)^{2}-4(3)(-8)}}{2(3)} \\  & =\frac{2\pm \sqrt{100}}{6} \\  & =\frac{2\pm 10}{6} \\  & =\frac{1\pm 5}{3}.\end{aligned}
$$

So, we get two solutions, ${x}_{1}=-\frac{4}{3}$ and ${x}_{2}=2.$ Since we need $x>0$, our final answer is $x=2$ only.
